variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Advanced distributed training coordinates multiple accelerators so one model-training job can exceed the memory or throughput of a single device. It partitions the batch, model state, layers, sequence, or experts, then uses communication collectives to keep those partitions consistent.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Assign deterministic work
pairs.detail: Partition examples or tokens by data-parallel rank.
pairs.explanation: Partition examples or tokens by data-parallel rank. Every sample should have an intentional owner, including the final uneven batch.

pairs.label: Compute local tensors
pairs.detail: Run the local model partition and produce activations, losses, and gradients for the rank's assigned work.
pairs.explanation: Run the local model partition and produce activations, losses, and gradients for the rank's assigned work.

pairs.label: Exchange required state
pairs.detail: All-reduce gradients, all-gather parameters, reduce-scatter shards, or send activations between pipeline stages according to the chosen layout.
pairs.explanation: All-reduce gradients, all-gather parameters, reduce-scatter shards, or send activations between pipeline stages according to the chosen layout.

pairs.label: Update and commit progress
pairs.detail: Apply a logically consistent optimizer step, advance the data position, and periodically publish a recoverable checkpoint.
pairs.explanation: Apply a logically consistent optimizer step, advance the data position, and periodically publish a recoverable checkpoint.

variants.hint:

Compute local tensors: Run the local model partition and produce activations, losses, and gradients for the rank's assigned work.

Exchange required state: All-reduce gradients, all-gather parameters, reduce-scatter shards, or send activations between pipeline stages according to the chosen layout.

variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Data parallelism
pairs.detail: Replicate the model, assign different examples to each rank, and synchronize gradients.
pairs.explanation: Replicate the model, assign different examples to each rank, and synchronize gradients. It is the simplest option when one complete training replica fits on every device.

pairs.label: Sharded data parallelism
pairs.detail: Shard optimizer state, gradients, and eventually parameters across data-parallel ranks.
pairs.explanation: Shard optimizer state, gradients, and eventually parameters across data-parallel ranks. FSDP and ZeRO reduce persistent memory at the cost of all-gather and reduce-scatter traffic.

pairs.label: Tensor parallelism
pairs.detail: Split matrix operations across a tightly connected group.
pairs.explanation: Split matrix operations across a tightly connected group. It helps when an individual layer is too large, but introduces communication within the layer's critical path.

pairs.label: Pipeline parallelism
pairs.detail: Place groups of layers on stages and stream micro-batches through them.
pairs.explanation: Place groups of layers on stages and stream micro-batches through them. It reduces per-stage state but creates bubbles when the pipeline fills, drains, or becomes imbalanced.

pairs.label: All-reduce
pairs.detail: Reduce corresponding values from all ranks and return the reduced result to every rank.
pairs.explanation: Reduce corresponding values from all ranks and return the reduced result to every rank. DDP commonly uses it to synchronize gradient buckets.

pairs.label: Reduce-scatter
pairs.detail: Reduce values across ranks while leaving each rank with only its assigned shard.
pairs.explanation: Reduce values across ranks while leaving each rank with only its assigned shard. Fully sharded training uses it for gradients.

pairs.label: All-gather
pairs.detail: Collect each rank's shard so participants can temporarily reconstruct the parameters required for a module's computation.
pairs.explanation: Collect each rank's shard so participants can temporarily reconstruct the parameters required for a module's computation.

pairs.label: Point-to-point send
pairs.detail: Move activations and gradients between pipeline stages.
pairs.explanation: Move activations and gradients between pipeline stages. Stage imbalance and too few micro-batches leave visible idle bubbles.

variants.prompt: What is the central correctness invariant of a synchronous distributed training step?
options: Every rank contributes according to the intended batch and synchronization contract before one coherent update is published
Every GPU reports the same utilization percentage
Each rank can apply a partial optimizer update independently
Checkpoint storage is faster than GPU memory
variants.explanation: Distributed execution may partition work, but the logical optimizer step must still represent the intended data and synchronized state. A failed partial step must not be published.

variants.prompt: Why can one missing or reordered NCCL collective call stall the other ranks?
options: Collectives require all participating ranks to enter compatible operations in the same order
NCCL writes every checkpoint to one GPU
All-reduce operates without process groups
Pipeline stages never communicate
variants.explanation: A collective is a group operation. Peers wait for the expected participants and operation ordering, so divergent control flow can produce an indefinite wait.
